source: Indian Express Plus special issue, “Election Commission of India: lapses and challenges”, PDF dated 5 October 2026, 80 pages, supplied by the site owner and not redistributed. Page numbers are the issue’s own.

rows.title: No one else may do an ERO’s work
rows.quote: “statutory functions of ERO, DEO and CEO (were) to be strictly exercised by them and no one else”

rows.title: The software must not limit the ERO
rows.quote: “ensure that IT system is made in a manner that ERO’s discretion to act in any manner is not restricted”

rows.title: ECINet launched
rows.quote: “On January 22, the Election Commission of India (ECI) launched ECINet”

rows.title: Flagged electors to be heard
rows.quote: “those affected be allowed ten days to submit documents or objections and be heard”

rows.title: Goa asks for a way to reverse decisions
rows.quote: “the required rollback/ reversion functionality, including the document re-upload option, has still not been provided in the system”

rows.title: Goa writes again
rows.quote: “there are 97 cases, in which the roll back option is required”

rows.title: Two emails and a letter
rows.quote: “no response has been received”

rows.title: “Most urgent”
rows.quote: “The matter is most urgent and requires immediate necessary action”

rows.title: Still no reply
rows.quote: “is still awaited”

rows.title: The list of 97
rows.quote: “it is requested that necessary action may be taken to include these electors in the Final Electoral Roll of SIR 2026”

rows.title: “IT system cannot block”
rows.quote: “IT system cannot block necessary action as per the directions of SC”

rows.title: Goa’s final roll, without the 97
rows.quote: “On February 21, the final roll was published. The Indian Express checked all 97 names against it.”

rows.title: Sandhu: decisions without the Commission
rows.quote: “many communications go out in the name of the ECI but they do not have the approval of the Commission”

rows.title: Joshi says the same
rows.quote: “several communications are disseminated in the name of the ECI without the requisite approval of ‘the Commission’”

rows.title: Joshi: Form 6 is fixed by law
rows.quote: “cannot be altered without making amendments in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960”

rows.title: Sandhu agrees
rows.quote: “On May 19, his colleague on the panel Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred with Joshi on file.”

rows.title: Joshi asks for an audit
rows.quote: “no one, except the concerned statutory authorities, has credentials to make any change in the (voter) database”

rows.title: The Form 6 change is reported
rows.quote: “On July 12, The Indian Express first reported on the new declaration in Form 6”

rows.title: Sandhu backs the audit
rows.quote: “improve the system”

rows.title: Oversight of the IT division removed
rows.quote: “Within hours, Garg changed the work allocation without consulting the Commission”

rows.title: Both write to the Cabinet Secretary
rows.quote: “In a move without precedent, the two Commissioners each wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary”

rows.title: The order is set aside
rows.quote: “Sandhu and Joshi jointly set Garg’s order aside”

rows.title: Sandhu: the Form 6 change is illegal
rows.quote: “must be removed immediately so that young and would-be first time voters, who are otherwise eligible, can register themselves”

rows.title: Sandhu: officers shut out of the roll
rows.quote: “doesn’t have any legal authority to restrict proper and complete access and freedom to operate, as given by law”

rows.title: The full Commission meets
rows.quote: “the CEC and the two ECs met, their first full meeting in four months”

rows.title: The investigation is published
rows.quote: “There was no response.”

rows.title: The Commission replies
rows.quote: “Differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution”

rows.title: The Goa account is published
rows.quote: “8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out”

rows.title: Nine decisions
rows.quote: “it announced nine decisions that addressed, point by point, several of the concerns recorded by the two Commissioners”

rows.title: A drive for those left out
rows.quote: “a special drive shall be undertaken … for the enrolment of left out and young/first time eligible electors”

rows.title: ECINet launched
rows.quote: It was built in strict accordance with the law, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar said. It would “enhance transparency, credibility and public trust”, said Seema Khanna, the Director General of IT in the Commission.

rows.title: The software must not limit the ERO
rows.quote: With the SIR underway in 12 states and UTs, and the IT division putting EROs onto a new module for issuing notices and holding hearings, Sanjay Kumar wrote to Khanna, asking her to “ensure that IT system is made in a manner that ERO’s discretion to act in any manner is not restricted”.

rows.title: Goa asks for a way to reverse decisions
rows.quote: the system had no rollback option that would let the EROs reverse it. Requests for the same had been coming from the field since January 22. On February 11, Goa Electronics Limited, the state agency that supports the CEO’s office on the software, wrote to the CEO and to Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), the Commission’s vendor (pp. 53 to 54) … The CEO forwarded it to Delhi the same day, to the Senior Deputy Election Commissioner in charge of Goa, Gyanesh Bharti, with Khanna copied. (p. 54)

rows.title: Sandhu on decisions taken without the Commission
rows.quote: Sandhu recorded that the IT division “has developed many new modules and portals in the last few months” without any being brought to his knowledge or presented to the Commission. “I have come to know about new developments from media only,” he wrote. He asked that Khanna be directed to keep all members of the Commission briefed and obtain “all necessary approvals” before undertaking any activity. (pp. 33 to 34)

rows.title: Joshi asks for an audit
rows.quote: proposed an audit, with an outside expert from the IITs, … Joshi proposed two checks. One committee would periodically review the systems and certify that only the statutory authorities had the credentials to change the voter database. A second committee would check whether ECINet complied with the law and ensure that any policy or procedural changes to ERONet and ECINet were brought before the Commission.

rows.title: Sandhu calls the Form 6 change illegal
rows.quote: On August 13, referring to The Indian Express report, Sandhu wrote to the Deputy Election Commissioner and the Director General in charge of IT, with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Joshi copied on the note. … the “unauthorised/ illegal changes in Form-6 on the portal” had not been removed

rows.title: Sandhu says officers are shut out of the roll
rows.quote: Their powers, he said, had been “curtailed by centralised control of ERONet at DG(IT) level”. “It is strange,” Sandhu wrote, that responsibility for the electoral roll lay with these statutory authorities while “access control has been centralised by DG(IT)”. … Sandhu directed full access “be given immediately”. He also asked the DG (IT) to certify, based on confirmations from all CEOs, that statutory authorities across states and Union Territories had full access to ERONet and could perform their duties without restrictions.

rows.title: The Goa account is published
rows.quote: The Indian Express sent a questionnaire to Seema Khanna, who heads the division as EC’s DG IT, asking why the rollback facility was not enabled for Goa before the final roll. There was no response. (pp. 50 to 51)

rows.title: Nine decisions
rows.quote: If field officers need more flexibility in the system, it will be provided. (p. 60) … “any further flexibility” field officers needed “will be made operational” in the software. (p. 69)

rows.title: A drive for those left out
rows.quote: The letter conveys the hearing change to the states, and is copied to the DG (IT) “for making necessary changes in ECINet”.

rows.title: Section note: who sets the permissions
rows.quote: Since January, every electoral roll in the country has sat on ECINet, the platform the Commission launched to bring its systems together, and its roll-management module, ERONet. What an ERO can do on it is decided by permissions set in the Commission’s IT division in Delhi. (p. 49) … What the software allows is controlled centrally by Khanna’s division in New Delhi. (p. 32, ECINet article)
